answer: Root each identity in a juniper enclave key: one key per device, unclonable, so one root cannot be copied into n clones. Trust grows only along a vine of real delegations, and branching dilutes it: splitting one vine into n branches cuts each branch's weight by more than 1/n. Each identity must also earn a jade seal via a sequential, time-locked task that cannot be parallelized or outsourced, and linked seals burn together on misbehavior. Cloning thus pays n roots and n seals for less than one identity's influence: cost superlinear, reward sublinear, sharing impossible.
